description.value: The study examined how anticipatory brain activity before emotion reappraisal relates to subsequent amygdala activity and success in reducing negative affect.

spans.text: The present results serve as the first investigation of mediated relationships among anticipatory brain activity and subsequent self-reported emotion regulation success.

value: if anticipating reappraisal enhances regulatory success, then we should find that anticipatory activation of reappraisal- or affect-related regions leads to larger drops in negative affect via down-regulation of subsequent amygdala responses to aversive images.

if anticipating reappraisal diminishes regulatory success, then we should find that anticipatory activation of reappraisal- or affect-related regions leads to smaller drops in negative affect via a failure to down-regulate subsequent amygdala responses to aversive images.

spans.text: On one hand, if anticipating reappraisal enhances regulatory success, then we should find that anticipatory activation of reappraisal- or affect-related regions leads to larger drops in negative affect via down-regulation of subsequent amygdala responses to aversive images.
